title: Alaska Glacier and Northern Lights Adventure

scenario.description: Solo adventure traveler planning 8-day Alaska trip from New York to see glaciers, northern lights, and wildlife. Must coordinate multiple activities with weather dependencies, seasonal timing, and Anchorage/Fairbanks transfer logistics. A key glacier tour gets cancelled due to weather, forcing replanning of a multi-day itinerary.

dynamic_events.description: Your Day 4 Prince William Sound glacier kayaking tour from Anchorage has been cancelled due to severe weather conditions and rough seas. This was a full-day guided excursion (8 AM - 6 PM) with round-trip transportation included. Your options: (1) Rebook the glacier kayaking tour for Day 5 morning (conflicts with your planned transfer to Fairbanks for northern lights viewing), OR (2) Substitute with a Matanuska Glacier guided hiking tour that includes round-trip transportation from Anchorage and returns by 4 PM, keeping an evening transfer to Fairbanks viable, OR (3) Skip glacier touring entirely and add an extra day in Fairbanks for better northern lights chances. Each option has different implications for your Anchorage departure timing, Fairbanks hotel booking, and northern lights viewing schedule.
resolution_requirements: Choose between 3 options with different trade-offs
Option 1 (Rebook Day 5): Delays Fairbanks arrival and loses one northern lights viewing night
Option 2 (Substitute tour): Different glacier experience (hiking vs kayaking), guided transportation included, shorter activity, keeps Fairbanks schedule intact
Option 3 (Skip glacier): Violates 'must see glaciers' hard constraint unless alternative glacier viewing arranged (e.g., flight tour, different ground tour)
Adjust Anchorage departure timing and Fairbanks arrival expectations based on the new glacier option
Update Fairbanks hotel check-in date if choosing Option 1
Ensure 'must see glaciers' constraint still met with any option
Verify total cost stays within $3500 budget (tour substitutions may have different prices)

expected_challenges: Two-city Alaska itinerary with long drive (Anchorage to Fairbanks = 6 hours) creates scheduling dependencies
Weather-dependent activities common in Alaska require backup planning
Must balance three 'must-see' requirements (glaciers, lights, wildlife) with weather constraints
Anchorage departure timing and Fairbanks arrival depend on which glacier option is chosen
Northern lights viewing is seasonal and weather-dependent (Sept is shoulder season)
Activity costs in Alaska are high (tours $150-400), budget pressure is real
Remote locations mean limited backup options if primary activities cancelled
notes: HARD task because: (1) Two remote Alaska cities with long inter-city transfer timing dependencies, (2) Three mandatory hard constraints (glaciers/lights/wildlife) creating tight scheduling, (3) Weather cancellation forces choice between three imperfect options with cascading effects, (4) Anchorage-to-Fairbanks transition timing depends on the chosen glacier option, (5) Northern lights viewing is time-sensitive (limited nights available), (6) Nature/adventure focus makes this realistic and exciting, (7) Tests ability to re-optimize a multi-day itinerary while preserving hard constraints. This is 'hard' due to remote location complexity and multiple interdependent activities, not artificial complexity.
